question: In Newfoundland and Labrador, my child turns five in December of the upcoming school year. Does being four in September automatically make the child ineligible for kindergarten?
generated_answer:
No, being four in September does not automatically make the child ineligible for kindergarten. The eligibility is based on the child's age by the end of the school year, not the start. If your child turns five by the end of the school year (June 30), they are eligible for kindergarten. However, if they turn five after June 30, they would be eligible for kindergarten the following year.

For example, if your child turns five in December 2023, they would be eligible for kindergarten in September 2023, as they would be five by the end of the 2023-2024 school year (June 30, 2024). If they turn five in January 2024, they would be eligible for kindergarten in September 2024, as they would be five by the end of the 2024-2025 school year (June 30, 2025).

It's always a good idea to check with your local school board or school for specific eligibility criteria, as they may have additional requirements or considerations.
